_about: Every feel number for game mode, read with Registry.tune("path.to.value", fallback). Test bench mode (lane B6) ignores "motors" and uses the actuator "bench" figures in parts.json instead. "standin" drives lane A1's box walker only; lane A2's gait generator adds its own block. Units are in the key names.

physics._about: air_density kg/m3 and drag_cd_area_m2 (drag coefficient x frontal area, a 3 x 2.4 m box-ish body with legs ~ 7 m2) give the mechs' quadratic air drag (lane A3 part 4), replacing Godot's default 0.1/s damping.

motors._about: Game-mode magic motors per joint kind: far stronger and faster than any real actuator, for the anime feel.

air._about: Lane A3 part 4 (Emerson 2026-09-30: air movement from real physics only). Leg-swing turning (standin_mech.gd _air_legs): the legs sweep outstretched up to swing_max_deg at swing_deg_s (accel swing_accel_deg_s2), tuck in to tuck_scale of their reach over tuck_s, return tucked, untuck; the body turns the other way by conservation of angular momentum. Legs keep their angular momentum and hand it back on landing. deadband_deg: aim error ignored. yaw_lead_deg: how far the aim may lead the body.

feet._about: Lane A2 part 4: a planted foot tilts to lie flat on the ground under its sole, at most max_tilt_deg; a planted foot more than reseat_m above or below where the ground now is under its sole takes a step to re-seat (as after a landing).

skid._about: The slide (lane A3 part 4): above min_speed_m_s the slide trigger breaks grip by its depth; friction is the feet's kinetic friction for non-player mechs (the player's is Settings > Slide friction); grip returns over recover_s after letting go.

recover._about: Lane A2 part 3: below 2 grounded legs, drive/turn/steady are off entirely by design (a bad landing angle should punish a jump), so nothing recovered a mech that tipped or wedged against terrain and settled near-still (results/A2.md: long_walk's tries 1 and 2, against a slab corner and a rock). stuck_speed_m_s tells a real fall (still moving) apart from stuck (not); stuck_delay_s must pass before ramp_s brings in _steady's proportional righting torque and an unstick_accel_m_s2 shove. Checked and deliberately not covered: a mech that stays fully grounded but rams an obstacle -- calibrated against the same slab -- was not actually stuck, plain reverse already frees it since drive/turn are never disabled while on_ground.

juggernaut._about: Overrides on top of "standin" (scripts/mech/juggernaut_mech.gd deep-merges this over the standin block) for the real Model 2's much bigger legs, tuned to refs/anime-motion/ANALYSIS.md (lane A2 part 2 and 3). "step" is the walk timing (0.5 s cycle, duty about 0.62: swing_s = 0.5 * (1 - duty)); "step_run" applies instead while sprinting (duty about 0.3-0.35, so a longer swing relative to the same drift-triggered stance: swing_s = 0.5 * (1 - 0.325)), matching the anime's faster, lower-duty run gait. "gun" rises at rest and levels while moving (the plan's one exception to "no independent gun traverse"): about 40 deg parked, the field pose everywhere else. "run_stance" widens the stance, drops the ride height and pitches the nose down while running (ANALYSIS.md's measured run pose: "very low and level, stance wide... does not bob", m19's own numbers "drop 0.28 m, -6 deg"); "skid.brace_out_m" adds the same widen while skidding (the anime's outward-braced turn), on top of run_stance's if both are true at once. Both are a symmetric widen on every leg, not biased toward the turn's outside specifically -- reasoned simplification, not asymmetric per ANALYSIS.md's exact description (results/A2.md).

run_stance._about: Lane A3 part 4: drop 0.28 m and -6 deg together lowered the front 0.46 m, exactly the belly's clearance, so the pod dragged at every gallop (Emerson's 'scraping'). Now 0.12 m and -2.5 deg: still low and level, 0.25 m left under the front.

suspension._about: Lane A3 part 4: the belly sits 0.46 m above flat ground at rest (measured on the chassis colliders); crouch + run-stance drop together stop at max_drop_m so 0.15 m stays under it.

feet._about: Lane A3 part 4, the 70 km/h gallop: with the run splay a front foot reaches only ~0.8 m ahead of its rest spot but ~3.7 m behind it (rears the mirror), so at speed each stride is centred in the leg's real range (rears gathered 1.5 m forward, fronts 1.2 m back) and may reach 1.7 m either side of that, leaving ~0.3 m for a step that waits on its partner: at 19.5 m/s the swing is 0.174 s. Part 5 (item 4): foot targets stay inside target_reach of the leg's reach; a planted foot past overreach, or closer than min_reach to its hip (horizontally), steps at once; a swinging foot is kept min_reach clear of its hip.

drive._about: Lane A3 part 4 (Emerson: 'I don't like how slow it is'): gallop ~70 km/h (run_m_s 19.5), walk 9 m/s; acceleration up to accel_m_s2 but never more than the legs' peak drive power (peak_power_w 600 kW, a power pack a 350 kg battery can feed in bursts), so 0-50 km/h takes about 1.3 s.
drive._sprint_about: Lane A4 (Emerson 2026-10-01: sprint should work well side to side and backwards): the legs splay to all four corners, so the gallop works in any direction; sideways the stride is shorter (the hips swing less across than along) and backwards the rear legs lead, so about 75% and 70% of the forward gallop.

jump._about: Lane A2 part 5, Emerson: the game-mode jump should be way better and more game-like (bench mode stays the physics test). Higher launch, a forward leap along the stick scaled by charge (the heavier fall went in lane A3 part 4: gravity only in flight), and a short grace time after leaving the ground so a jump released mid-stride still fires.

upright._about: Lane A2 part 5, Emerson: normal play must not tip the spider over (no flail animations yet). Game mode only, gated by Balance assist: past keep_deg of lean a righting torque (rad/s2 per unit of lean past keep, capped at 3x) and spin damping; keep_air_factor of that in the air.

jump_bench._about: Test bench charge jump: launch energy is what the leg actuators can really deliver over their stroke.

aim._about: look_* is where the pilot looks (camera and wire anchors, lane A3 part 4); pitch_* is how far the body tilts after it on its legs.

combat._about: Lane A3 part 4 (Emerson: real physics only): the recoil game/air scales (x6, x24) and the recoil_point_share are gone; recoil is Ballistics.recoil_impulse along the bore line. impact_push_scale is 1: a hit pushes with the projectile's own momentum.

grapple._about: Lane A3 part 4: the dart goes where you aim (crosshair), inside the sub-arms' reach (arm_pitch_min/max_deg, arm_yaw_deg either side); assist_cone_deg is the small nudge toward a marked grapple point near the aim. Cable: a one-sided spring (stiffness per tonne of mech, damping ratio), no game scale; the winch and cable limits are on weapons.json wire_anchor. The pull acts at the real socket.

foot_dust._about: Dust thrown by each planted foot at a run (lane B4, scripts/look/foot_dust.gd). Pairs are [at min_speed_m_s, at full_speed_m_s] and blend between. surfaces: how much dust each ground gives (sounds.json surface names; metal is a steel deck or a mech, none). kick_back: how far back against the run the puff leans (0 straight up). camera_fade_m: a puff is clear nearer the camera than the first and full beyond the second. soft_ground_m: how softly it meets the ground. max_live: puffs alive at once, for frame rate.

photo._about: Photo / inspect mode (scripts/camera/photo_mode.gd): the orbit camera's limits and speeds.
